wins.text: Daily sales grew 12.4% YoY to $34.9M per day in Q1, marking the third consecutive quarter of double-digit growth
Operating margin improved 20 bps YoY to 20.3%, driven by SG&A leverage declining from 25% to 24.3% of sales despite incentive comp reload
Customer sites spending $50K+/month grew 16.3% YoY to ~2,900 sites, now accounting for over half of total sales at 21% revenue growth; average monthly sales per site increased $5,700
Operating cash flow of ~$378M represented 111% of net income, with ROIC improving 180 bps on a trailing 12-month basis to 31%
FMI device agreements signed at ~7,000 in Q1 (~110/day, +8% YoY), expanding active device base ~6% and driving ~45% of Q1 sales through FMI, up 150 bps YoY; international sales grew ~24% in March

risks.text: Gross margin came in ~40 bps below internal Q1 target and 50 bps below prior year as tariff-related cost increases moved through the P&L faster than pricing actions; realized pricing of ~3.5% YoY was insufficient to offset inflation
Tariff and trade policy uncertainty (IEEPA, Section 122, Supreme Court rulings) created a 'slog' in customer pricing conversations, delaying price increases and creating execution risk into Q2

Branded product categories (safety, cutting tools) face margin pressure from aggressive supplier cost increases of 6-8%+ that are difficult to pass through quickly due to contractual pricing terms of 30-60 days
Customer mix remains a structural gross margin headwind as growth skews toward larger accounts with lower gross margins, though positive at the operating margin level

Commodity-driven cost spikes (e.g., nitrile gloves up sharply due to Middle East petroleum dynamics) adding unpredictable inflation pressure; CFO noted unusual difficulty forecasting supplier cost increases vs. a typical year

guidance_items.detail: Full-year 2026 net CapEx expected at ~$320M, approximating ~3.5% of consensus net sales, focused on hub capacity, FMI devices, automation and IT
Management confirmed high-20s incremental margin expectation for full year remains intact despite Q1 gross margin shortfall; SG&A leverage expected to continue
Pricing expected to reach 5-8% cumulative peak around mid-year; price/cost neutrality targeted but timing of recovery from Q1 shortfall not specified; Q2 acknowledged as challenging

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: Whether new contract signings are linked to slower pricing execution (i.e., new business being priced in at lower margins)
Competitive behavior — whether rivals are holding prices artificially low to win business
Section 232 tariff changes and their specific impact on Fastenal's fastener business
